blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Fine-tuning foundation models on financial data has a wide range of applications, including identifying event types from news, monitoring risk and compliance language, and answering questions over filings and earnings calls. In this setting, the main challenge is to improve task performance without degrading the generalization capabilities of the model. In this paper, we present an extensive set of ablations for fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We compare three training regimes: (1) response-only LoRA, where the supervised response is the label alone; (2) single-adapter reasoning, where reasoning traces from a teacher model are included alongside the labels in the training loss; and (3) dual-adapter composite training, where separate LoRA adapters are trained on traces and labels. Response-only LoRA improves in-domain performance and leaves general capabilities near those of the frozen model. The in-domain change is largest for calibration and argmax accuracy. Under single-adapter reasoning, the in-domain metrics remain behind those of the response-only regime, while MMLU-Pro can rise slightly and the other retention benchmarks stay within ordinary variation. Dual-adapter composite training remains on the same side of this comparison and yields no further gain. Finally, we compress the teacher traces by summarizing them before training, and show that shorter summaries move calibration toward the response-only regime without reaching it.

blocks.en:
LoRA makes domain specialization computationally cheap. Yet specialization is only
useful if the adapted model keeps its broad capabilities. After fine-tuning, it should
still generalize to unseen problems, follow instructions, and express calibrated
uncertainty. Retaining these capabilities is especially challenging for classification-like tasks
with long inputs. In this setting, the adapter must learn a specialized decision
boundary while preserving the base model’s general reasoning.

blocks.en:
One potential solution to this problem is to distill knowledge from a larger, more capable model
(the teacher ) into the student during fine-tuning. Teacher-generated
reasoning traces show the intermediate steps that lead to the final answer and thus
provide far more supervision per example than the answer alone. However, these traces
also contain repetition, hedging, self-correction, and prose specific to the teacher,
and training on full traces asks the student to reproduce all of it. Reasoning traces
therefore offer a rich domain signal, but whether the student keeps its general
capabilities depends on how this signal changes the model during fine-tuning.

blocks.en:
Training on traces from a larger model is slow, because each example contains many
more tokens than the answer alone. This makes trace-based fine-tuning hard to run in
low-resource settings, which are the main use case for LoRA. One way to address this
is to summarize the teacher traces before they are used to fine-tune the student,
so that the student is trained on only a fraction of the original tokens. However,
the choice of compression method and compression ratio is critical: too much
compression can remove the information that makes the traces useful and leave
fine-tuning with little to learn from.

blocks.en:
In this study, we examine how supervising with the response (or label) alone, compared with
supervising with a teacher reasoning trace, affects domain performance and capability
retention. We study two ways of incorporating traces into LoRA fine-tuning. The first is a
blended loss, where a single adapter is trained on a weighted combination of the trace loss
and the label loss, with a weight that controls how much each part contributes. The second
is dedicated adapters, where the rank budget is split between one adapter for the trace and
one for the label, and the two are merged into a single update at inference. The trace is
either the full teacher trace or a summary of it, and we vary the degree of compression.
All comparisons use matched training configurations, so that a consistent trend can be
separated from a single favorable setting.

Our main contributions are as follows: 1. We present a systematic study of reasoning supervision in LoRA fine-tuning
for a financial classification task. We use a dataset of 200K examples as our main training set. 2. To this end, we first build a strong response-only baseline by tuning the LoRA hyperparameters of a
Qwen3-8B [ 2 ] model on our dataset. 3. We study how to incorporate the reasoning traces of a larger teacher model into

weight that balances the two terms. 4. We propose a composite adapter that uses separate LoRA modules for the labels and

fixed rank budget. 5. We summarize the teacher traces before training and ablate the effect of several
compression levels. 6. We evaluate all configurations on both the in-domain task and a set of retention
benchmarks, so that gains on the target task can be weighed against losses in

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) updates a frozen model through trainable low-rank
matrices [ 1 ] , while QLoRA extends this setup to quantized base
models [ 3 ] . A small trainable footprint does not, however,
guarantee retention. Compared with full fine-tuning, LoRA often learns less and
forgets less, with rank controlling the tradeoff [ 4 ] ;
forgetting also grows with the number of updated parameters and optimization
steps [ 5 ] . With sufficient capacity, broad layer
coverage, and appropriate tuning, LoRA can nevertheless match full
fine-tuning [ 6 ] . This dependence on the training regime
motivates evaluating adaptation and retention jointly rather than treating LoRA
as a capability-preserving baseline.

blocks.en:
Our reasoning supervision can also be understood as sequence distillation.
Classical knowledge distillation matches softened teacher and student
distributions [ 11 ] ; sequence distillation replaces that
distribution with the teacher’s highest-scoring decoded
response [ 12 ] . Our sampled traces are likewise hard sequence
targets. Prior rationale distillation has trained rationale generation and label
prediction as separate tasks [ 13 ] , whereas we train on a
single response containing a trace followed by its label. We treat the trace as
a verbalized rationale rather than as a faithful account of the teacher’s
internal process.

blocks.en:
Which rationales help depends on both the student and the objective. The useful
level of granularity varies with student capacity, and stronger teachers do not
always yield better students [ 14 ] . Existing methods have
separated rationale and answer learning [ 15 ] or combined LoRA
experts trained on different reasoning tasks [ 16 ] . Our
narrower intervention trains two always-active additive factors on a single
response containing a trace and a label. The trace factor receives both losses,
the label factor receives only the label loss, and the total rank is matched to
the single-adapter control. Because the factors merge into one static update,
the intervention changes the training procedure rather than the inference
architecture.

Trace length introduces a related efficiency tradeoff. Prior work shows that
full traces give the highest accuracy, while compressed traces reduce training
and inference cost and usually outperform truncation at the same
length [ 17 ] . We therefore compare full traces with semantic
summaries at several compression levels, rather than assuming that shorter
traces are inherently better or worse.

blocks.en:
Figure 1: Overview of the staged protocol.
The teacher (Qwen3-32B) labels 200K FinHeadlineMix headlines and generates a reasoning trace for each.
We then fine-tune the student (Qwen3-8B) with LoRA in four stages:
(1) response-only LoRA, trained on the label alone over a hyperparameter grid,
(2) single-adapter reasoning, trained on the trace and the label with the blended loss of Eq. ( 1 ),
(3) dual-adapter composite LoRA, which splits the rank budget between a trace adapter and a label adapter,
and (4) summarized traces, which repeats Stages 2 and 3 with teacher-generated summaries at target lengths of 25%, 50%, and 75%.
In every stage, each run uses three seeds and is evaluated on the in-domain task and the retention benchmarks.
A run is carried to the next stage when it outperforms the frozen model on every task. If none does, we fall back to the run with the highest average retention score among those that beat the frozen model on the in-domain tasks.

blocks.en: 3 Methods of LoRA Supervision
blocks.zh: 3. LoRA监督方法

blocks.en:
In this section, we first describe the models and dataset used in our study, along with
practical considerations such as hyperparameter tuning. We then describe the supervision
methods used in LoRA fine-tuning. Finally, we present the staged protocol that organizes
our study.
blocks.zh:
在本节中,我们首先描述我们的研究所使用的模型和数据集,以及
超参数调试等实际考虑. 然后我们描述监督
LORA微调中使用的方法。 最后,我们提出分阶段的 协议,组织
我们的研究。

blocks.en: 3.1 Dataset Generation and Model Architecture
blocks.zh: 3.1 数据集生成和模型架构

We study LoRA fine-tuning in the financial domain. To this end, we fine-tune Qwen3-8B [ 2 ] on a training set of 200K examples whose inputs are headlines from the FinHeadlineMix

blocks.en: 3.2 Response-only LoRA

blocks.en:
In the first stage, we apply LoRA fine-tuning to the student using only the labels from our dataset. This
allows us to assess how training on the labels affects domain performance and retention on MMLU-Pro, GPQA, and IFEval.
In this stage, we also perform hyperparameter tuning to find the best
settings, which we then use in the subsequent stages. This establishes how much domain utility and
calibration the available labels can provide while preserving the model’s held-out capabilities.
Across all experiments, the LoRA rank is r = 32 r=32 .

blocks.en: 3.5 Summarized Traces
blocks.zh: 3.5 总结追踪

blocks.en:
In the fourth stage, we repeat our reasoning experiments with summarized traces, for both the single and the composite adapter.
Following [ 17 ] , we summarize each trace with our 32B teacher model to a target token budget. To this end, each trace
is wrapped in a prompt that asks the model to rewrite it as a summarized version of a given length.
We ablate several length ratios to measure the effect of summarization on the in-domain and retention performance of the fine-tuned model.
In each case, we allow the model to generate up to 10 % 10\% (with a constant offset) more tokens than the target,
so that the summary is not cut off before it is complete.
The implementation details and the results of this ablation are presented in Section 4.6 .
blocks.zh:
在第四阶段,我们用总结的痕迹重复我们的推理实验,无论是单子还是复合适配器。
接下来的[17],我们用我们的32B师范模型总结每一个追踪到目标符号预算. 为此,每个追踪
被包裹在一个提示中,该提示要求模型将其重写为特定长度的概要版本.
我们降低若干长度比率,以衡量总和对微调模型的域内和保留性能的影响。
在每种情况下,我们允许模型产生最高为10%的10-Q(恒定抵消)比目标多的代币,
以免摘要在完成之前被切断。
第4.6节介绍了实施细节和这项削减的结果。

blocks.en: 3.6 Sequential Experimental Design
blocks.zh: 3.6 序列实验设计

blocks.en:
Comparing fine-tuning schemes is only meaningful if differences in accuracy reflect the schemes themselves rather than the hyperparameters chosen for any one of them.
However, a full hyperparameter search is impractical because the search space grows exponentially.
We therefore organize the study in stages, each building on the runs selected in the previous one.
We first evaluate the frozen model without fine-tuning and use it as the primary baseline.
The fine-tuning experiments then proceed in four stages:
blocks.zh:
比较微调方案只有在准确性差异反映方案本身而不是为其中任何一个方案选择的超参数的情况下才有意义。
然而,全面超参数搜索是不切实际的,因为搜索空间呈指数增长.
因此,我们分阶段安排这项研究,每项研究都以上一份研究报告中选择的成绩为基础。
我们首先评估被冻结的模型,不作微调,并将其作为主要基准。
然后,微调实验分四个阶段进行:

blocks.en:
Stage 1. We run response-only LoRA (Section 3.2 ) over the selected hyperparameter grid and keep the runs that satisfy the selection criterion. Details of the hyperparameter selection are given in Appendix A.1 . Stage 2. Starting from these runs, we train single-adapter reasoning LoRA (Section 3.3 ) over a range of λ \lambda values in Eq. ( 1 ) and keep the top runs, satisfying the selection criterion. Stage 3. For each run kept in Stage 2, we train dual-adapter composite LoRA (Section 3.4 ) with equal, trace-heavy, and label-heavy splits. We repeat these experiments at the λ \lambda values adjacent to the selected one, so that the final comparison does not depend on the exact λ \lambda chosen in Stage 2. Stage 4. Finally, we repeat the experiments of Stage 2 and Stage 3 with summarized traces, where each trace in the training data is replaced by its summary (Section 3.5 ).
We ablate different summarization levels in this stage. -Figure 1 summarizes the above stages in our study.

blocks.en:
At every stage we apply the same rule: a run is kept only if it outperforms the frozen baseline on all tasks, both in-domain tasks and retention (general-capability) tasks.
We use this rule to satisfy an important practical consideration: a model that gains in-domain accuracy at the cost of its general capabilities is of limited use.
Using one rule throughout also keeps the comparison fair across schemes.
When no run satisfies this rule, we fall back to the run with the highest average retention score among those that outperform the baseline on all in-domain tasks.
Full task details are given in Section 4.1 .
blocks.zh:
在每一个阶段,我们都适用同样的规则:只有当运行超过所有任务的冻结基线时,运行才会被保持,包括域内任务和保留(一般能力)任务。
我们利用这一规则来满足一个重要的实际考虑:一种以一般能力为代价而提高域内准确性的模式是有限的。
在整个过程中使用一条规则也保持了各方案之间的公平比较。
当没有运行符合这个规则时,我们又回到运行中,在完成所有域内任务的基线时,平均保留分最高。

blocks.en: 4 Experimental Results
blocks.zh: 4 实验结果

blocks.en:
This section presents the experimental results of our study.
For each experiment stage, we first describe the setup and methodology,
then report the results and discuss the findings.
blocks.zh:
本节介绍我们的研究结果。
对于每个实验阶段,我们首先 描述设置和方法,
然后报告结果并讨论调查结果。

blocks.en: 4.1 Training and Evaluation Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 培训和评价设置

blocks.en:
All experiments fine-tune a single base model, Qwen3-8B, with LoRA on a dataset of headline inputs from FinHeadlineMix [ 18 ] , annotated by the teacher model (see Section 3.1 ).
We train every model with AdamW [ 19 ] for a single epoch, repeat each configuration with three random seeds, and report the mean and standard deviation across seeds. The training hyperparameters are ablated in Section 4.3 .
We evaluate every fine-tuned model along two axes:
(i) In-domain and (ii) Retention .
blocks.zh:
所有实验都微调了单基模型Qwen3-8B,由FinHeadlineMix[18]提供头条输入的数据集上LORA,由师范模型作注释(见第3.1节.
我们用亚当W[19]训练每个模型,为一个时代,用三个随机种子重复每个配置,并报告种子之间的平均和标准的偏差. 训练高参数仪在第4.3节中减速。
我们按照两个轴线来评估每一个精细的模型:
(一)域内和(二)留置.

blocks.en:
We measure in-domain performance on a held-out, class-stratified set of 10,000 financial-headline event-classification examples.
We report greedy accuracy (“Acc”) and macro-F1 (“F1”) over the 35 event classes.
To assess calibration, we additionally report the negative log-likelihood (“NLL”) and Brier score [ 20 ] (“Brier”)
of the model’s label distribution, together with argmax accuracy (“Acc. argmax”).
Argmax accuracy scores each of the 35 class strings as a teacher-forced continuation of the prompt
and counts a prediction as correct when the gold class receives the highest likelihood.
Unlike greedy accuracy, which parses the label from the model’s greedy generation and therefore also penalizes formatting failures,
argmax accuracy isolates how well the model’s class-token distribution ranks the correct label (it is computed from the same distribution as NLL and Brier).
blocks.zh:
我们用10 000个金融头条事件分类实例来衡量域内业绩。
我们报告35个事件类别中,贪婪的准确性(“Acc”)和宏观F1(“F1”)。
为了评估校正,我们还报告负对数(NLL)和Brier分数[20](“Brier”)
该模型的标签分布,加上正格马克斯精度( " Acc. argmax " )。
argmax 精度分数为 35 个课弦中的每个, 由 师资 强制 继续 。
并计算出黄金类获得最大概率时的预测正确性。
与贪婪的精度不同,精度从模型的贪婪一代中描述出标签,因此也惩罚格式化的失败,
argmax精度隔离了模型的类键分布排列正确标签(它是从与 NLL 和 Brier 相同的分布中计算出来的)。

blocks.en:
We measure retention on three public benchmarks: MMLU-Pro [ 21 ] for broad multi-task knowledge and reasoning, GPQA-Diamond [ 22 ] (“GPQA”) for graduate-level scientific reasoning,
and IFEval [ 23 ] (“IFEval”) for instruction following, for which we report prompt-level strict accuracy.
All evaluations use greedy decoding with the model’s thinking mode disabled and the same prompt template as in training,
so that scores are directly comparable across all fine-tuning configurations and against the untuned base model.
blocks.zh:
我们根据三个公共基准衡量保留情况:MMLU-Pro[21]用于广泛的多任务知识和推理,GPQA-Diamond[22](“GPQA”)用于研究生科学推理,
和用于以下指示的IFEval [23] (“IFEval”),我们报告这些指示的准确性是迅速的。
所有的评价都使用贪婪的解码 模式的思维模式被禁用 和相同的快速模板 在培训,
这样,在所有微调配置中,与未调试的基础模型相比,得分是直接可比的.

blocks.en: 4.2 Baseline Results
blocks.zh: 4.2 基线结果

blocks.en:
Table 1 reports the performance of the untuned base model (Qwen3-8B without fine-tuning) on all metrics.
Each evaluation is run three times, and we report the mean and standard deviation (std).
The largest run-to-run variation is on GPQA (std ≈ \approx 4.3%) among the retention benchmarks and on macro-F1 (std ≈ \approx 1.1%) among the in-domain metrics.
GPQA contains only 198 questions, so each one is worth roughly 0.5 percentage points, and the questions are difficult enough that the model sits near the decision boundary on many of them, so the
score moves noticeably.
Macro-F1 is similarly sensitive because it weights every class equally regardless of its size: for small classes, a few flipped predictions can shift that class’s F1 substantially.

表1汇报了未调整的基准模型(Quen3-8B不作微调)在所有度量衡上的性能.
每次评价进行三次,我们报告平均和标准差(std)。
在保留基准中,最大的从运行到运行的变化是GPQA(std \\\ 大约4.3%),在域内衡量标准中,宏观-F1(std \\\ 大约 1.1%)。
GPQA只包含198个问题,所以每个问题大约值0.5个百分点,而且问题难度很大,以至于模型在其中很多问题上坐落在决定边界附近,所以
分数明显移动。
Macro-F1同样具有敏感性,因为它对每个等级的权重是平等的,无论大小:对于小等级来说,几个翻转的预测可以大大地改变该等级的F1。

blocks.en: 4.3 Response-only LoRA Results
blocks.zh: 4.3 仅反应的LORA结果

blocks.en:
Response-only LoRA improves in-domain performance and leaves general capabilities near the frozen model. The in-domain change is largest for calibration and for which class the model ranks first. Greedy accuracy and macro-F1 move less.
We LoRA-fine-tune Qwen3-8B on this dataset with AdamW for a single epoch, and we ablate the LoRA scaling coefficient α \alpha , the peak and minimum learning rate, the AdamW β 1 \beta_{1} , and the number of warm-up steps (see Appendix A.1 for hyperparameter details).
We then select the top runs that outperform the frozen base model on all tasks, both in-domain and retention.
This criterion yields 5 runs for the 200K dataset, and these are the runs carried forward to Stage 2.

blocks.en:
In the fourth stage, we study the effect of training on summarized reasoning traces.
To construct length-controlled summaries, we compress each teacher-generated trace
with the teacher model itself (Qwen3-32B, greedy decoding) under a token-level length budget.
Given a trace of T T tokens and a target length ratio K ∈ ( 0 , 1 ] K\in(0,1] ,
we instruct the teacher to rewrite the trace as a condensed version of approximately ⌊ K ⋅ T ⌉ \lfloor K\cdot T\rceil tokens,
where ⌊ ⋅ ⌉ \lfloor\cdot\rceil denotes rounding to the nearest integer.
The summary must preserve the essential reasoning steps, the decisive evidence, and the final category choice,
while keeping the first-person deliberative style of the original trace (the exact prompt and implementation details are given in Appendix A.5 ).
To prevent runaway generations without forcing mid-sentence truncation,
we cap the output at 1.1 ⋅ ⌊ K ⋅ T ⌉ + 32 1.1\cdot\lfloor K\cdot T\rceil+32 tokens, i.e., 10 % 10\% above the target length plus a fixed margin of 32 32 tokens.

5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented a systematic study of reasoning supervision in LoRA fine-tuning for a financial classification task,
comparing response-only training with two ways of using teacher reasoning traces:
blending the trace into the loss of a single adapter and splitting the rank budget between a trace adapter and a label adapter.
We also studied the effect of summarizing the traces before training.
All regimes were compared under a staged protocol with matched hyperparameters and evaluated on both the in-domain task and retention benchmarks.
blocks.zh:
我们对LORA的推理监督进行了系统研究,对财务分类任务进行了微调,
将只针对应答的培训与使用教师推理痕迹的两种方法进行比较:
将"微量"混入单位适配器丢失后,将分级预算从"微量适配器"和"标签适配器"中分出.
我们还研究了总结训练前的痕迹的效果。
根据分阶段协议,所有制度都与匹配的超参数进行比较,并对域内任务和保留基准进行评价。

blocks.en:
Response-only LoRA is the regime that improves in-domain performance while leaving general capabilities near the frozen model.
The gain is largest for calibration and for which class the model ranks first. Adding a full teacher trace does not extend this gain.
The in-domain metrics stay behind the response-only runs, MMLU-Pro can rise slightly,
and the other retention benchmarks stay within ordinary variation.
Splitting the rank across a trace adapter and a label adapter does not change this comparison.
The allocation only affects NLL, which worsens as more rank is given to the label adapter.
Summarizing the traces moves calibration back toward the response-only regime without reaching it,
lowers IFEval by a few points, and reduces accuracy and macro-F1 at intermediate summary lengths.
The composite adapter follows the single adapter at every summary length.
blocks.zh:
只反应的LORA是改善域内性能,同时使一般能力接近被冻结的模型的制度.
增益最大的是校正,对于哪个等级,模型排名第一. 加上完全的老师追踪并不能延长这一收益.
MMLU-Pro可以略微上升,
其他留存基准保持不变。
将等级分出一个微量适配器和一个标签适配器不会改变这种比较.
分配只会影响NLL,随着标签适配器的分级增加而恶化.
总结一下这些痕迹 回到只反应的状态
将IFEval降低几分,并降低中间摘要长度的精度和宏-F1.
复合适配器按每个总长跟随单个适配器.

blocks.en:
Several extensions remain open.
The same comparison can be repeated at other data scales and on other classification-like financial tasks, such as risk and compliance language or questions over filings.
Attaching a trace to only part of the training examples would test whether the MMLU-Pro lift can be kept at a smaller cost to calibration.
Decision models in the style of Jev [ 24 ] return one choice from a fixed list together with a probability.
They address the same problems and have not been compared with these LoRA regimes.
Finally, all of our experiments use AdamW, and the comparison could be repeated with other optimizers.
blocks.zh:
几个延期仍然开放。
其他数据尺度和其他类似分类的财务任务,如风险和合规语言或对备案的问题,也可重复同样的比较。
仅将部分培训实例附后,将检验MMLU-Pro升力能否以更小的成本保持校准.
Jev [24] 风格中的决定模型从固定列表中返回一个选择并带有概率.
它们涉及同样的问题,没有与LORA制度相比较。
最后,我们所有的实验都使用亚当W,与其他优化者可以重复比较.
